newsitem.title: CANADA: Great Lakes Gas plans major pipeline expansion.
newsitem.headline: Great Lakes Gas plans major pipeline expansion.

text.p: Great Lakes Gas Transmission LP, a pipeline that carries Canadian natural gas through the northern United States, said on Thursday it planned to construct about 1,000 miles of pipeline and add compression equipment in a US$2.5 billion expansion.

Great Lakes, equally owned by Calgary-based TransCanada PipeLines Ltd and Coastal Corp of Houston, said the project would add about two billion cubic feet a day of capacity to the system, a 100 percent increase.

The proposal, part of TransCanada's major expansion push dubbed the Nexus project, is the latest of a spate of plans to boost export capacity for Canadian gas, which together are valued at several billion dollars.

Great Lakes, whose system extends to eastern Michigan from southern Manitoba via Minnesota and Wisconsin, said the expansion plan represented more than 90 percent of capacity requests received in response to its recently concluded open season.
The project was expected to be in service no later than the winter of 1999-2000, the company said.

"This additional service of up to two BCF per day would represent a 100 percent increase in transportation capacity held by shippers utilizing Canadian-sourced gas," Derek Henwood, chief executive of Detroit-based Great Lakes, said in a statement.
"However, the ultimate expansion volume will depend on timely receipt of valid precedent agreements and regulatory approvals."
Under the plan, the expansion would run the length of the current mainline system and serve markets mostly in the U.S. Northeast and eastern Canada.
An application to build the project was expected to be filed with the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission in September, the company said.
The schedule envisaged construction starting in the winter of 1998-99, Great Lakes said.
